describe: make a whole game where you catch falling things
guide: A new thing needs three pieces in three places, and with only two it does nothing: create it once ABOVE the game loop, move it INSIDE the loop, and draw it inside the loop AFTER screen.fill(...). Give its speed, size and colour named constants at the top.
For a catching game, make things fall from the top, and when the player touches one, add a point and send it back to the top.
guide_scene: Build it with game_object, one call for each thing: the player's look (name player), and the things to catch (a drawing, with count, moves: down and touch: collect -- catching one then scores a point). Open Nest draws and moves each one every frame.
Only what game_object has no word for -- lives, a timer, a game over -- is edit_file.
report: I added $what, and a score in the top left corner. $touch Move with the arrow keys to catch them.
It's a catching game now: $what. $touch The score is in the top left.
There are $what, and a score to count your catches. $touch
teach: Each block moves down a little every frame. When one touches the player, the score goes up and the block goes back to the top.
_note: needs_words: a whole game is only built when the child asks for a game. Measured (SPIKES.md section 25N): as one part of a longer message, 'add some walls i have to get around' was read as this recipe at 1.00.
